headline: Egor Surin to sign with Predators following 2026-27 KHL season
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Egor Surin will sign with the Predators after the 2026-27 KHL season, with his agent, Dan Milstein, confirming the Russian star will move to North America next season. Nothing changes for Nashville this year, so the useful question is what kind of team he is joining.

So far this season, NSH sits at 6-4-5 with 17 points through 15 games. Expected goals measures the quality of chances, and the Predators have taken 49 percent of it overall, essentially even. At 5-on-5 that slips to 46 percent, so they're being outchanced in the most common game state. They've scored 2.4 fewer goals than their chances suggest. Goaltending has held the standings together: goals saved above expected, which compares saves to what an average goalie would make on the same shots, is plus 4.3. The power play creates 0.69 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.59, neither a strength nor a hole. Surin's arrival won't fix any of that this season, but a team that is middling at even strength and leaning on its goalie is the kind that needs fresh skill to arrive on schedule. We'd treat him as a 2027-28 story, and watch how Nashville's 5-on-5 numbers hold up before then.
